messages.subject: [statnet_help] Please Distribute: Call for Best Article on Political Networks
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Please Distribute: Call for Best Article on Political Networks
messages.body_plain:
The Political Networks Section of the American Political Science  
Association calls for nominations for 'The Political Ties Award' for  
the best peer-reviewed journal article on political networks in the  
past two years.  Articles must have been published between April 1,  
2010 and March 31, 2012 (according to either the online publication  
date or the in-print publication date).  Articles may be published in  
any peer-reviewed journal, but but the substance of the article must  
address political networks.  Nominations should be sent to Michael  
Heaney at mheaney@umich.edu by April 1, 2012.  Self nominations are  
welcome.

--

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Question about ERGM term
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am having trouble thinking about the appropriate ergm term for the following model: the probability of a tie Yij as a function of i's value of a continuous variable X and j's value of a continuous variable Z. The argument I am trying to test is that individuals with high levels of X should affiliate with individuals with high levels of Z. Specifically, X is an index of physical maturity and Z is an index of delinquent behavior. So, the question is whether individuals with low physical maturity are more likely to form ties with individuals who engage in delinquency. Any help would be much appreciated.

Thanks,


--
Jacob T.N. Young, PhD
Assistant Professor
School of Criminology and Criminal Justice
Arizona State University
Jacob.Young.1@asu.edu<mailto:Jacob.Young.1@asu.edu>

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Interpreting Goodness of fit
messages.body_plain:
I would appreciate some help on the interpretation of some of the details of GOF diagnostics.  I have estimated an ERGM on a network of 85 neighborhood councils, and the results look good.  I have statistically significant estimates of coefficients, and they remain stable with slightly different model specifications.  By increasing the MCMC samples I have reduced the MCMC standard errors to at least an order of magnitude smaller than the estimated standard errors.  The GOF diagnostics (which are too large to attach) show that 95% bands of the simulated networks based on the model are in line with the observed network, and the traces of coefficient estimates do not show any trends.

My main concern is the interpretation of the information on dependence factors, enough burn-in, and enough samples.  In that table, I have many coefficients for which I am told there is not enough burn in and not enough samples.  How should that information affect my interpretation of the GOF diagnostics?  I have scanned through the archives of this listserv and Socnet and have not found much that is on point.

Thanks

Chris

~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

messages.subject: [statnet_help] betweenness calculation for "large" networks?
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I tried to use the betweenness function on a network with 5535 nodes and
got the following error message:

"Error: evaluation nested too deeply: infinite recursion /
options(expressions=)?"

This network is not connected and contains several components. I also tried
to use the largest component, but got the same error message.
I also checked the max number of geodesics between any two nodes, which is
around 5X10^6. Is this the major reason?

Any ideas on how to solve this problem?

Thanks!

Best,

Mengxiao

messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

The information on dependence factors, enough burn-in, and enough 
samples is given to you through the CODA library (when you use the 
mcmc.diagnostics() function). This small article will probably help you:

Plummer, M., Best, N., Cowles, K., & Vines, K. (2006). CODA: Convergence 
diagnosis and output analysis for MCMC. R News, 6(1), 7?11.

See also the raftery.diag help page:
library(coda)
?raftery.diag

Best regards,
Victorin

messages.subject: [statnet_help] set edge attributes memory problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi, Jennifer.  A matrix can't be of class network; do you mean that you 
are using an adjacency matrix?  That aside, if you are assigning that 
matrix as an attribute to each edge, you are making as many copies of it 
as you have edges in the graph.  That could easily explain the growth in 
your data size.  (Do you mean instead to assign a numerical attribute to 
each edge?  That's rather different from assigning a network or 
adjacency matrix to each edge....)

Hope that helps,

-Carter

messages.subject: [statnet_help] set edge attributes memory problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi Carter, thanks for the reply.  My intention is to use an adjacency matrix (which I converted to class "network" for use in the ergm package) as a RHS variable in an ERGM.  I intended to use the edgecov term with this adjacency matrix, and thought that I needed to assign the adjacency matrix as attributes of the edges of the LHS adjacency matrix (also class 'network').  But your explanation about why this blew up makes sense and I think that I've misunderstood the appropriate way to use dyadic/adjacency variables on the RHS of an ERGM.  Can you provide some further advice about how to properly specify this model?

For example, I want to estimate an ERGM where the dependent variable is an adjacency matrix of cosponsorship  connections between legislators.  I have a few structural terms (m2star, triangle) to use, plus some nodecov and nodematch terms to use from an attribute file.  But I also want include a dyadic measure of caucus connections between legislators on the RHS.  The cosponsorship data are directed and the caucus data are not.  I *thought* I was going to do this by making the caucus data an edge attribute of the cosponsorship data, then use edgecov(caucus) in the ERGM, but clearly this is not correct. I can provide some sample code if this explanation is not sufficient to describe what I'm trying to accomplish.

I greatly appreciate any/all advice!

Best,
Jennifer
